ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Biliary pancreatitis without cholangitis

A 39-year-old woman has acute gallstone pancreatitis. She is afebrile and improving; bilirubin is falling and there is no evidence of persistent duct obstruction or cholangitis. Which statement about urgent ERCP is most accurate?

  1. It replaces all later gallbladder management
  2. It is always contraindicated if cholangitis develops
  3. It is not routinely indicated in this presentation
  4. It is mandatory for every gallstone pancreatitis episode
  5. It is required to establish pancreatic enzyme elevation
Answer and explanation

It is not routinely indicated in this presentation

Routine urgent ERCP is not recommended for biliary pancreatitis without cholangitis or persistent obstruction.

Option explanations

It is not routinely indicated in this presentation: Routine urgent ERCP is not recommended for biliary pancreatitis without cholangitis or persistent obstruction.

It is mandatory for every gallstone pancreatitis episode: The indication depends on associated obstruction or cholangitis.

It is required to establish pancreatic enzyme elevation: ERCP is not the test for serum lipase elevation.

It replaces all later gallbladder management: Duct intervention does not automatically address the gallbladder source.

It is always contraindicated if cholangitis develops: Cholangitis can create an urgent indication for biliary drainage.
